title: The report and the notebook
goal: Use Lesson 1 on the case notebook: find the six B09 jars.
story: The report names batch B09. Same idea as Lesson 1, new names: the practice table logbook is now jars, the case notebook.

dictionary.means: the case notebook (made up for this game): a table of 12 jars with the columns jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Julia's word: a DataFrame.
a name that holds the batch named in the report
a rule before the comma keeps the rows where it is true: the jars on tray T-C, every column. Julia's word: a boolean mask (logical indexing).
a rule inside a column's brackets keeps the values where it is true: the ids of the jars on tray T-C. Julia's word: a boolean mask on a Vector.

challenges.prompt: Show the six B09 jars from the case notebook (the table jars), with all four columns: jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. The name case_batch holds the batch, B09. Any row order is fine.
hints: Rows go before the comma in the square brackets, columns after it. Keep a row when its batch_id matches case_batch.

feedback.pass: You kept the six B09 rows. Next: how many of them had springtails?

errors.say: This chapter uses the case notebook, jars. It is the lesson's logbook under a new name.
B09 is text, so it needs quotes. Or use case_batch, which already holds it.
Check the spelling. The table is jars, and the batch name is case_batch.
The four columns of jars are jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Check the column name after the dot.
To ask a question of every jar, write .== with two equal signs and a dot. One = would give a name to something.

challenges.prompt: How many of the B09 jars had springtails? Show one number.
hints: Take the detected column, keep only the B09 rows, then add up the trues.

feedback.pass: 5 of the 6 B09 jars had springtails.
feedback.wrong: Show one number for the B09 jars only. All twelve jars, or a table of rows, is not that number.

errors.say: This chapter uses the case notebook, jars. It is the lesson's logbook under a new name.
B09 is text, so it needs quotes. Or use case_batch, which already holds it.
Check the spelling. The table is jars, and the batch name is case_batch.
The four columns of jars are jar_id, batch_id, tray_id and detected. Check the column name after the dot.
Julia gave one answer for the whole column. Write .== with a dot, so it asks every jar.
Inside the square brackets put a true-or-false question about every jar, not a single value.

close.finding: In the notebook, 5 of the 6 B09 jars have springtails.
close.next: Next: Lesson 2 shows how to count by tray.
